title: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head L (Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment)

sections.label: Budget cut for Head L
sections.summary: A motion proposes reducing the total sum allocated for Head L of the Estimates by $100.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head L of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sections.label: Coastal protection and land projects
sections.summary: T5, Tekong Polder and Long Island are described as projects protecting low-lying areas and ensuring Singapore's place in a changing climate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: T5 will be built on land topped up to 5.5 metres above main sea level, higher than the rest of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Tekong Polder is 1.2 metres below sea level and protected by six metres seawalls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: And to remind ourselves what long-term planning means, the "Long Island" project was first mooted in the 1991 concept plan 30 years ago as an integrated plan to protect the East Coast with an integrated mix of projects to ensure coastal flood protection, rainwater harvesting and land supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: These are all novel ideas, underwritten by billions in Government commitment to protect our low-lying areas and ensure Singapore's continued place in a changing climatic world.

sections.label: Rainfall and aquaculture climate effects
sections.summary: More intense rainfall tests flood resilience and warming seas affect aquaculture, with annual rainfall rising about 83 millimetres per decade since 1980.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More intense rainfall test flood resilience and warming seas affect aquaculture stability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We have observed increased in average annual rainfall and the frequency of heavy rainfall with annual rainfall rising about 83 millimetre per decade since 1980.

sections.label: Singapore seafood farms numbers
sections.summary: As of 2023, Singapore had 98 sea-based and 33 land-based seafood farms, mostly in near shore coastal waters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of 2023, Singapore had 98 sea-based and 33 land-based seafood farms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Most farms are concentrated in near shore coastal waters, where sea space and environmental conditions impact farm viability.

sections.label: Third Climate Change Study projections
sections.summary: Singapore's Third Climate Change Study provides climate projections for Singapore and the region up to the end of the century.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore's Third Climate Change Study (V3) provides climate projections for Singapore and the region, attempting to cover the present till the end of the century.

sections.label: Uneven global emissions reductions
sections.summary: Given uneven global emissions reductions, adverse climate impacts could come earlier and more extreme than projected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the uneven pace of emissions reductions globally, we could indeed face adverse climate impacts earlier than projected, and with more devastating and extreme effects than initially anticipated.

sections.label: Heat stress management measures
sections.summary: MOM's Workplace Safety and Health Council strengthened heat stress guidelines for outdoor workers, and MND piloted cool coatings and urban design measures to reduce heat build-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) Workplace Safety and Health Council has strengthened heat stress management guidelines for outdoor workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) has piloted cool coatings and incorporated urban design measures to enhance airflow and reduce heat build-up in estates.

sections.label: Cross-Ministry heat resilience framework
sections.summary: A cross-Ministry heat resilience framework would align workplace heat stress guidelines with building design standards, estate planning and industrial operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, anchor a cross-Ministry heat resilience framework that aligns workplace heat stress guidelines with building design standards, estate planning and industrial operations.

sections.label: Heat-resilient industrial precinct pilot
sections.summary: A heat-resilient industrial precinct or campus could be piloted, measuring workers' productivity outcomes, infrastructure durability, maintenance frequency and energy consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To operationalise this, we can pilot a heat-resilient industrial precinct or campus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Importantly, we measure not just workers' productivity outcomes, but also infrastructure durability, maintenance frequency and energy consumption.

sections.label: Groups facing higher heat exposure
sections.summary: Children, seniors, residents in smaller flats with less ventilation or without air-conditioning, and outdoor workers in construction, landscaping and food delivery face greater heat exposure.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Children, seniors, residents living in smaller flats with less ventilation or households without air-conditioning will feel the impact of high heat temperatures more severely.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Outdoor workers, including Singaporeans and migrant workers in construction, landscaping and also food delivery roles, will face prolonged exposure to heat and rain as part of their livelihoods.

sections.label: Estate heat mitigation measures
sections.summary: Measures could include sheltered and ventilated linkways, cooler waiting areas, and heat mitigation for common corridors and lift lobbies, with MSE and NEA asked to identify hotspot blocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This could include	sheltered and ventilated linkways, cooler waiting areas near common facilities and heat mitigation for common corridors and lift lobbies where residents gather.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I would also ask MSE and the National Environment Agency (NEA) to consider working together with the Housing and Development Board (HDB) and Town Council to identify what I call “hotspot blocks” using simple indicators.

sections.label: Baseline outdoor heat exposure estimate
sections.summary: A baseline estimate of outdoor heat exposure across sectors could support sector-specific guidelines, more enforcement at construction sites, and resources like rest areas and hydration access.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: If we are able to develop a baseline estimate of outdoor heat exposure across sectors, this would help us to strengthen our support for those who are facing higher heat risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This could include sector-specific guidelines, more enforcement in construction sites, or practical resources such as having rest areas, hydration access and work-rest protocols that account for real operating conditions.

sections.label: Singapore temperature rise rate
sections.summary: Singapore's mean surface air temperature rose about 0.25°C per decade from 1948 to 2024, roughly double the global warming rate, with days above 34°C and warmer nights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore's mean surface air temperature has risen about 0.25°C per decade between 1948 and 2024, roughly double the rate of global warming.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We now face days constantly above 34°C and warmer nights.

sections.label: NEA 2024 recycling statistics
sections.summary: NEA's 2024 statistics show only 5% of plastic and 8% of glass are recycled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to NEA's 2024 statistics, only 5% of plastic is recycled and 8% of glass.

sections.label: Extended Producer Responsibility packaging waste
sections.summary: NEA is exploring extending Extended Producer Responsibility to broader packaging waste, especially plastics, a third of domestic waste, with mandated recycled content requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, I welcome NEA's exploration of extending Extended Producer Responsibility to broader packaging waste, particularly plastics, which constitute a third of our domestic waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Paired with mandated recycle content requirements, this would address the economic barriers that currently make only 5% plastic recycling viable.

sections.label: Larger recycling bin collection schedule
sections.summary: For estates with larger side loading recycling bins, collection is scheduled twice a week, and these bins fill up quickly even outside the festive season.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the estates where the larger side loading recycling bins are located, collection is scheduled for twice a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These larger bins fill up quickly, even outside the festive season.

sections.label: Metrics for waste collection frequency
sections.summary: The passage asks what metrics NEA uses to determine whether appointed public waste collectors should increase collection frequency for the larger bins.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What metrics does NEA use to determine whether appointed public waste collectors should increase collection frequency for the larger bins?

sections.label: Blue bin contamination problem
sections.summary: Recycling rates are improving, but contamination of blue bins, especially with food waste, remains a persistent problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our recycling rates are improving, but yet contamination of blue bins, especially with food waste, remains a persistent problem.

sections.label: Widening waste reduction laws
sections.summary: Asks if the Ministry will widen the Resource Sustainability Act and Good Samaritan Food Donation Act for stronger waste reduction and data reporting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, will the Ministry consider widening the Resource Sustainability Act and the Good Samaritan Food Donation Act's scope to introduce stronger upstream waste reduction obligations and improve data reporting requirements to better support circular outcomes?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Are there plans to set mandatory packaging waste reduction targets, rather than relying mainly on recycling rates?

sections.label: Plastic waste and recycling rate
sections.summary: States plastics are the largest waste stream by volume and the plastic recycling rate fell from 11% in 2013 to 4.6% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Plastics are now the largest waste stream by volume, yet our plastic recycling rate has fallen significantly from 11% in 2013 to a mere 4.6% in 2024.

sections.label: Recycling plastics economically challenging
sections.summary: A Singapore Environmental Council study found waste managers see plastic recycling as economically challenging because there is no local demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A study by Singapore Environmental Council found that waste managers see it as economically challenging to recycle plastics because there is no local demand for it.

sections.label: Expanding producer responsibility and recycled content
sections.summary: Suggests expanding extended producer responsibility to all packaging and mandating minimum recycled plastic content in bottles, packaging and goods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We must continue to find ways to reduce our reliance on incineration when plastics recycling ceases to be commercially viable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We can consider expanding extended producer responsibility beyond beverage containers to cover all packaging, including e-commerce mailers and food delivery containers, building on mandatory packaging reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To create demand for recycled plastics, the Government can also mandate that plastic bottles, packaging and goods must contain a minimum percentage of recycled plastics.

sections.label: Public bodies buying recycled plastic
sections.summary: Says schools, hospitals and agencies can build demand by purchasing only plastic bins, road barriers, pipes and park furniture made from recycled plastic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Schools, hospitals and agencies can build demand by only purchasing plastic bins, road barriers, pipes and park furniture made from recycled plastic.

sections.label: Carrier bag charge and climate vouchers
sections.summary: Reports the Disposable Carrier Bag Charge cut bag usage by up to 80% and asks for latest data, and notes climate vouchers were enhanced to $400.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Introduced in mid-2023 at larger supermarkets, this initiative has already shown promising results, with at least large supermarket operators having reported a reduction in bag usage by up to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This nudge has encouraged many to bring reusable bags, cutting down on plastic waste that clog our landfills and oceans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, as we approach the three-year anniversary of the Disposable Carrier Bag Charge, I would like to ask the Ministry: what is the latest data on the scheme's overall effectiveness in reducing disposable bag consumption across Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Second, regarding climate vouchers under the Climate Friendly Households Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This scheme has been a valuable tool, providing vouchers for energy and water efficient appliances, and it was recently enhanced with an additional $100, bringing the total to $400 per eligible household and extended to private properties until 31 December 2027.

sections.label: Beverage Container Return Scheme launch
sections.summary: The Beverage Container Return Scheme launches 1 April 2026, run by BCRS Ltd, giving a 10-cent refund per plastic and metal container returned at over 1,000 machines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Third, the upcoming Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS) set to launch on 1 April 2026.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This deposit-refund system for plastic and metal beverage containers, managed by BCRS Ltd, promises to boost recycling rates with a 10-cent refund per container returned at over 1,000 reverse vending machines island-wide at launch, aiming to double that within the first year.

sections.label: Shift to Food Story 2
sections.summary: Singapore has shifted from "30 by 30" to Food Story 2.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: First, we note that Singapore has shifted from "30 by 30" to Food Story 2.

sections.label: 2035 fibre and protein targets
sections.summary: By 2035, the aim is to produce 20% of fibre needs and 30% of proteins.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: For example by 2035, for us to produce 20% of our fibre needs and 30% of our proteins.

sections.label: Imported food and food waste
sections.summary: Almost all food in Singapore is imported, people complain about high food cost, and Singapore produces over 800,000 tonnes of food waste yearly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Last, while almost all the food in Singapore is imported and people are complaining about high food cost, Singapore produces more than 800,000 tonnes of food waste every year.

sections.label: Rice MOUs and agri-tech zone
sections.summary: The Minister cited rice MOUs with Vietnam and Thailand and the Brunei-Singapore Agri-Tech Food Zone as strengthening trade assurance beyond normal commercial transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister has cited examples such as the rice memoranda of understanding (MOUs) with Vietnam and Thailand, and the Brunei-Singapore Agri-Tech Food Zone, which will strengthen trade assurance beyond normal commercial transactions.

sections.label: Fermentation and novel protein production
sections.summary: Controlled-environment fermentation and novel protein production require limited land and are less exposed to climate variability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Controlled-environment fermentation and novel protein production require limited land and are less exposed to climate variability.

sections.label: 30 by 30 goal revised
sections.summary: The 30 by 30 goal was replaced with revised 2035 targets, with high-tech farms shutting down and 2024 output at 8% fibre and 26% protein.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: Mr Chair, in November last year, it is with a measure of regret that we note the "30 by 30" goal – producing 30% of our nutritional needs by 2030 – has been replaced with revised targets for 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: Our local agri-food sector has faced severe headwinds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: We have seen high-tech farms shut down and a quarter of our sea-based farms exit the industry in 2024 due to rising costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: The statistics are sobering: in 2024, we produced only 8% of our fibre and 26% of our protein.

sections.label: Open cage fish farms lost
sections.summary: Between 2023 and 2024, a quarter of open cage fish farms were lost, leaving 74 remaining.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Between 2023 and 2024 alone, we lost a quarter of open cage fish farms and 74 remain.

sections.label: Farmers struggle with cheaper imports
sections.summary: Farmers said they can meet production targets but struggle to compete with cheaper imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Farmers shared that while they can meet production targets, they struggle to compete with cheaper imports.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story 2 unveiled
sections.summary: In November 2025, Minister Grace Fu unveiled the Singapore Food Story 2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In November 2025, Minister Grace Fu unveiled the Singapore Food Story 2.

sections.label: Pioneer hawkers subsidised rent
sections.summary: Pioneer hawkers, about 30% of cooked food stallholders, pay heavily subsidised rent of about $300 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our Pioneer hawkers, who currently still make up around 30% of cooked food stallholders, pay heavily subsidised rent at about $300 per month.

sections.label: Pioneer hawker stall transfer
sections.summary: In 2024, Mr Koh Poh Koon said pioneer hawkers' stalls can be transferred to immediate family members at the same low rent of about $300 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In 2024, then-Senior Minister of State for MSE Mr Koh Poh Koon said that the stalls of our pioneer hawkers can be transferred to immediate family members at the same low rent of about $300 per month.

sections.label: Stretching out fee increase
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a rise from $300 to $1,250 could be stretched over 12 years instead of three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, rather than a sharp jump from $300 to $1,250 in three years, could we stretch it out over 12 years instead?

sections.label: Work permit holders as stall assistants
sections.summary: The passage urges MSE to reconsider allowing work permit holders as stall assistants for stalls operating over 10 years, and notes budget meal participation is no longer mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, my view is that as long as the head of the stall is a Singaporean, physically present daily at the stall and producing familiar hawker food, it does not matter as much the nationality of his or her stall assistant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, to further support our long-serving hawkers manage their manpower needs and costs, I urge MSE to re-consider allowing work permit holders to work as stall assistants in our hawker centres, for stalls that have been operating for more than 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Chairman, earlier this year, the Government announced that participation in the budget meal programme by HDB coffee shops would no longer be mandatory, citing feedback from patrons and hawkers.

sections.label: Hawkers absorb discount costs
sections.summary: The passage states that discounts for Pioneer Generation, Merdeka Generation and certain CHAS cardholders are absorbed by the hawkers themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Further, the discounts offered to Pioneer Generation (PG), Merdeka Generation and certain the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) cardholders are absorbed by the hawkers themselves.

sections.label: Discount cost on Government
sections.summary: The passage states the cost of this discount should be imposed on the Government, not the hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Importantly, the cost of this discount should not be imposed on the hawkers, but on the Government instead.

sections.label: Town Councils paying to catch chickens
sections.summary: The passage states one Town Council may pay $200 to catch one chicken and another pays $400 for a similar outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: From my research, one Town Council may effectively be paying $200 to catch one chicken and another Town Council pays $400 to catch another one chicken for a similar outcome.

sections.label: Coordinating standards and pooling demand
sections.summary: The passage states that if MSE and NEA coordinate standards, pool demand and strengthen shared capabilities, unevenness across estates can be reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: In summary, if MSE and NEA can coordinate standards, pool demand and strengthen shared capabilities, we can reduce the unevenness across estates and deliver a more consistent baseline of public health and liveability for residents across Singapore.

sections.label: Second-hand smoke deaths
sections.summary: The Global Burden of Disease 2023 study attributes at least one Singapore death to second-hand smoke, with climbing numbers, prompting a call to ban smoking at windows and balconies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: From The Global Burden of Disease 2023 study, at least one person in Singapore dies that is attributed to second-hand smoke and the numbers are climbing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: It is time to act decisively to protect Singaporeans from second-hand smoke.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: It is time to legislate and ban smoking at windows and balconies.

sections.label: AI enforcement camera sandbox
sections.summary: MSE is asked whether it will commission a sandbox pilot for AI-enabled cameras that mask interiors and faces and detect thrown objects or cigarettes at windows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: Will MSE commission a sandbox pilot for AI-enabled enforcement cameras?

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: This pilot using smart cameras could first, automatically and instantly mask the interiors of units and the faces of residents to ensure privacy; two, strictly detect specific motions, specifically the trajectory of an object being thrown or the lighting of a cigarette at the window interface.

sections.label: Support for young coastal advocates
sections.summary: The passage states their work strengthens coastal defence, builds regional stewardship and raises public awareness, and urges co-funding, grants and mentorship for young advocates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Their work strengthens coastal defence, builds regional stewardship and raises public awareness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I urge structured support through co-funding, grants and mentorship so young advocates can actively contribute to national planning.

sections.label: Projected climate hazard economic loss
sections.summary: Climate hazards are projected to cause economic loss of over a trillion dollars by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Climate hazards are projected to cause economic loss of over a trillion dollars by 2050.

sections.label: Sea level rise threats
sections.summary: Rising sea levels with high tides and extreme weather threaten to submerge a significant part of the country by the end of this century, causing major losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Rising sea levels, coupled with high tides and extreme weather events, threaten to submerge a significant part of our country by the end of this century, potentially causing major losses in property, our economy and human lives.

sections.label: Year of Climate Adaptation
sections.summary: Singapore will designate 2026 as the Year of Climate Adaptation and formulate its first National Adaptation Plan with citizens, businesses and civil society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Together, we must keep Singapore going as much as possible in step with the changing climate and recover as quickly as possible in the face of extreme weather events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will designate 2026 as the Year of Climate Adaptation to galvanise this collective effort on adaptation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Together with citizens, businesses and civil society, we will formulate Singapore's first National Adaptation Plan, our long-term strategy to build a climate-ready nation.

sections.label: Drainage improvement works
sections.summary: Drainage improvement works will be carried out at Bedok First Subsidiary Drain and Sungei Serangoon subsidiary drains, and 900 metres of Bukit Timah Canal will be completed this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For example, we will be carrying out drainage improvement works to Bedok First Subsidiary Drain and Sungei Serangoon Eastern and Western subsidiary drains to reduce flood risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will also complete drainage improvements to 900 metres of the Bukit Timah Canal between Rifle Range Road and Jalan Kampong Chantek this year.

sections.label: Coastal defence line
sections.summary: A continuous line of defence will be built around Singapore, and conceptual studies for the North-west Coast from Tuas to Lim Chu Kang are completed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: To protect our coastlines from rising seas, we will build a continuous line of defence around Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are pleased to share that we have now completed conceptual studies for the North-west Coast from Tuas to Lim Chu Kang.

sections.label: Coastal Protection Bill
sections.summary: The Coastal Protection Bill will be tabled for Second Reading, giving legislation and regulatory powers to implement the coastal protection plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This week marks an important step forward in our coastal protection journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We will table the Coastal Protection Bill in Parliament for Second Reading, which, when passed, will give us the legislation and regulatory powers to implement our coastal protection plan.

sections.label: Weather Science Research Programme
sections.summary: CAWRAS is implementing a $25 million Weather Science Research Programme to raise capability in weather forecasts and climate projections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: CAWRAS is implementing a $25 million Weather Science Research Programme, which will raise our capability in weather forecasts and climate projections.

sections.label: Partnerships and heat sensors
sections.summary: Partnerships allow exchange of scientific knowledge and climate science research collaboration, and the heat stress sensor network is expanding from nine sensors in 2023 to 20 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These partnerships allow us to exchange scientific knowledge and collaborate on climate science research.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We are expanding our heat stress sensor network from nine sensors in 2023 to 20 today and will install more sensors island-wide.

sections.label: Year of Climate Adaptation
sections.summary: MSE has designated this year as the Year of Climate Adaptation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   MSE has designated this year as the Year of Climate Adaptation.

sections.label: National Adaptation Plan inputs
sections.summary: Public inputs will shape the first National Adaptation Plan, to be published in 2027 and implemented in later years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Inputs from members of the public will shape our first National Adaptation Plan, which we will publish in 2027 and implement in the years to come.

sections.label: Year of Climate Adaptation
sections.summary: 2026 is designated the Year of Climate Adaptation, with calls for participation in the National Adaptation Plan and decisive adaptation action.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Climate adaptation is not merely about building sea walls along our coasts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It is also about enhancing the mental preparedness and response capabilities of our people and communities, so that our nation can remain calm and steadfast when facing increasingly volatile and extreme weather events.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Most of all, as a Singaporean, I would like our generation to be a source of pride for the future generations of Singaporeans, that we have done right by them, that with gumption and courage, we have the foresight to make the right strategic decisions to build a strong foundation for climate resilience for their future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: I call on all Members of this House and all citizens, businesses and civil society to participate fully in the formulation of our National Adaption Plan in the Year of Climate Adaptation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We must therefore take decisive action to adapt to the new realities we face.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Hence, we designated 2026 as the Year of Climate Adaptation.

sections.label: DTSS and water plants
sections.summary: Tuas Water Reclamation Plant and Tuas NEWater Factory will commission in phases from 2027, and Changi NEWater Factory 3 works are expected to finish in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)

sections.label: Heat Resilience Policy Office
sections.summary: MSE has established a new Heat Resilience Policy Office to tighten whole-of-Government coordination and enhance the heat resilience strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As climate change impacts intensify and heat continues to affect all segments of the society, we need to tighten whole-of-Government coordination and enhance our heat resilience strategy so that we holistically address all impacts of heat, including those to the economy and society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We are happy to announce that MSE has established a new Heat Resilience Policy Office.

sections.label: Heat Resilience R&D Programme
sections.summary: The RIE2030 Heat Resilience R&D Programme will be launched with two pillars and a $40 million Adapting to Heat Impacts Funding Initiative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This ensures that the measures under the Action Plan are backed by science.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will launch the RIE2030 Heat Resilience R&D Programme, to advance capabilities and investments in heat resilience research through two complementary pillars – one focusing on infrastructure interventions and the other on understanding and managing impact of heat on society.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As part of this programme, we will launch a $40 million "Adapting to Heat Impacts" Funding Initiative, which will step up research in emerging areas, such as heat impact and community heat resilience.

sections.label: Expanded eligibility for appliances

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Next month, we will expand its eligibility to include five-tick clothes dryers and induction stoves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since then, participating supermarkets have reported a 70% to 80% reduction in the number of bags issued at checkout.

sections.label: Scheme launch tagline Return Right

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In a few weeks, the scheme will launch with the tagline “Return Right”.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: With the scheme, we expect to recover over 16,000 tonnes of material every year for recycling.

sections.label: Supermarkets display beverage prices without deposit
sections.summary: Major supermarket operators collectively decided to display beverage prices on shelves without the 10-cent deposit, charged at checkout.

sentences.text: They have collectively decided to display beverage prices on shelves without including the 10-cent deposit, and reflect that the deposit will be charged at checkout.

sections.label: Return Right reverse vending machines deployment
sections.summary: Over 1,000 Return Right reverse vending machines are to be deployed by 1 April, increasing to 2,000 within the first year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Efforts are underway to deploy over 1,000 Return Right reverse vending machines (RVMs) by 1 April, where consumers can get their 10-cent deposit refunded via SimplyGo EZ-Link cards and concession cards and DBS PayLah!.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: At launch, there will be roving ambassadors to assist consumers in the use of the RVMs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will progressively increase the RVMs deployed to 2,000 within the first year as more containers with the 10-cent deposit mark enter circulation.

sections.label: One-time support for F&B operators
sections.summary: A one-time support of $500 per food shop on application will be provided to F&B operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: However, it will require additional effort and some operational adjustments for F&B operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will therefore provide a one-time support of $500 per food shop on application.

sections.label: Cameras and smoking prohibitions
sections.summary: Town Councils get two surveillance camera deployments monthly for high-rise littering, and NEA expanded smoking prohibitions to over 49,000 public places.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Under this initiative, each Town Council is provided with two surveillance camera deployments per month to enable faster and more targeted intervention for high-rise littering cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Since the pilot started in October 2025, 39 cameras have been deployed with a 30% catch-rate, an encouraging result from our closer collaboration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To reduce public exposure to second-hand tobacco smoke, NEA has progressively expanded smoking prohibitions to over 49,000 public places across Singapore, up from 32,000 in 2021.

sections.label: Rat enforcement and Wolbachia expansion
sections.summary: About 1,200 enforcement actions were taken for rat-related lapses in 2025, and Project Wolbachia will cover 740,000 households by March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: About 1,200 enforcement actions were taken by NEA and SFA against premises owners and managers for rat-related lapses in 2025, of which about 560 were for refuse management lapses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To suppress the mosquito population, NEA has also expanded Project Wolbachia, which will cover 740,000 households by March 2026, up from 580,000 households in April 2025.

sections.label: Singapore Food Story 2 pillars
sections.summary: The Singapore Food Story 2, announced by Minister Grace Fu, includes four pillars: diversify imports, grow local, stockpile and global partnerships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: A single-pillar approach, no matter how ambitious, cannot provide the food supply resilience that Singapore needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This brings us to the Singapore Food Story 2, which Minister Grace Fu announced in November last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: It includes four pillars: diversify imports, grow local, stockpile and global partnerships.

sections.label: Supporting food import industry
sections.summary: The Government will accredit new sources for meat and eggs, help importers with business matching, and establish regionalisation agreements with key sources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government will support the industry by accrediting new sources, for food of higher food safety concern, such as meat and eggs; we will help our local food importers with business matching; and safeguarding supply stability by establishing regionalisation agreements with key sources.

sections.label: Poultry imports during Brazil outbreak
sections.summary: During Brazil's Avian Influenza outbreak, poultry imports from accredited farms in unaffected regions were maintained rather than restricting all of Brazil.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For example, during Brazil's Avian Influenza outbreak last year, we maintained poultry imports from accredited farms in unaffected regions, rather than restricting imports from the whole of Brazil.

sections.label: Rice trade memoranda agreements
sections.summary: Two memoranda agreements on rice trade were signed with Vietnam and Thailand last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As the Member has mentioned, recent examples include the two memoranda agreements on rice trade signed with Vietnam and Thailand last year.

sections.label: Food stockpiles and disruptions
sections.summary: Singapore will stockpile essential food items like rice, having expanded stockpiles since COVID-19 to include frozen protein and canned vegetables covering all three food groups.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Chairman, even with our efforts to reduce the likelihood and impact of disruptions, it is still possible that we could face widespread disruptions where food cannot reach our borders for some time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: And this is why we will stockpile essential food items, such as rice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As shared in this House in November last year, since COVID-19, we have expanded our stockpiles to include frozen protein and canned vegetables to cover all three food groups – carbohydrates, fibre and protein.

sections.label: Local production targets fibre protein
sections.summary: Under Singapore Food Story 2, refreshed local production targets focus on fibre and protein types feasible to produce at scale in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Hence, our refreshed local production targets under Singapore Food Story 2, we are focusing on fibre and protein types that are feasible to be produced at scale efficiently in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: These are fresh leafy and fruited vegetables, such as xiao bai cai and tomatoes, beansprouts and mushrooms for fibre; and eggs and seafood for protein.

sections.label: Funding awarded to projects
sections.summary: Since its launch, $55 million has been awarded to nearly 150 projects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since its launch, we have awarded $55 million to nearly 150 projects.

sections.label: New ACT Fund 2 tranche
sections.summary: A new tranche of funding of $70 million under the ACT Fund 2 is announced, introducing the Industry Partnerships for Capability Transformation Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, I am announcing a new tranche of funding of $70 million under the ACT Fund 2.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: At the same time, it will introduce a new funding component – the Industry Partnerships for Capability Transformation Grant.

sections.label: National Broodstock Centre programme
sections.summary: In November 2024, the National Broodstock Centre and Hatchery Development and Recognition Programme was introduced to supply farms with high quality eggs and fingerlings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In November 2024, we introduced the National Broodstock Centre and Hatchery Development and Recognition Programme to supply our farms with high quality eggs and fingerlings, with higher survival and grow-out rates.

sentences.text: Five hatcheries have been recognised under the Hatchery Development and Recognition Programme and can now access quality seabass eggs and marine tilapia brooder fingerlings from the National Broodstock Centre.

sentences.text: For example, the sales for xiao bai cai under the "SG Farmers' Market" brand have increased about sevenfold since its launch in May 2024.

sections.label: Risk monitoring and aquaculture tools
sections.summary: A risk monitoring dashboard and food supply visibility tool developed with PSA BDP gives early warnings, and the Harmful Algal Bloom Prediction Model is being upgraded to integrate forecasted weather.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Our new risk monitoring dashboard and food supply visibility tool, developed with PSA BDP, provides early warnings of developments that may affect food imports and strengthens Singapore's upstream food supply chain visibility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For aquaculture, we are upgrading our Harmful Algal Bloom Prediction Model to integrate forecasted weather conditions for more accurate environmental predictions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This will alert farms ahead of anticipated events so that they can implement mitigation measures like aeration or emergency harvests to minimise stock losses.

sections.label: Government food supply measures
sections.summary: The Government will invest in the ACT Fund 2, expand the National Broodstock Centre, create offtake programmes with SAFEF and strengthen early warning systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government will continue doing our part – be it investing in the ACT Fund 2, expanding the National Broodstock Centre, creating offtake programmes with SAFEF and strengthening early warning systems.

sentences.text: Supermarkets should expand local produce shelf space, restaurants should join our Farm-to-Table Recognition Programme and food manufacturers should partner with SAFEF to develop local supply chains.

sections.label: Choosing local produce

sentences.text: Choose local produce even if it costs slightly more and be more flexible with our food choices during crises and shortages.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: That premium we pay for our local produce is our insurance for reliable food supply when things fail.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)

sentences.text: At an average of 128 kilogrammes of food waste per capita per year, and this is an increasing trend, Singapore ranks amongst the top 15 countries worldwide with highest food waste per capita.

sentences.text: The second clarification is in relation to the SG Eco Fund.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is heartening to hear from the Minister that $50 million granted since November 2020 has engaged more than 700,000 people on sustainability related efforts.

sections.label: Return Right deposit obligation

sentences.text: Even after 1 April, an F&B outlet can choose to sign up.

sentences.text: But if it has not yet signed up and is not on the list as a "Return Right" F&B outlet, then they have an obligation to charge the 10-cent deposit for the 10-cent deposit to follow the container with the customer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary

sentences.text: For example, they also provide cell-based seafood cultivation platforms like Umami Bioworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: They developed a joint-production agreement with the Japanese seafood producer Maruha Nichiro to develop and commercialise cell-cultivated tuna.

sections.label: Hawker stall rental transfer rules
sections.summary: Subsidised stalls transferred to immediate family pay subsidised rent, while other transfers get three years to stagger to market rent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: He raised questions and concerns about rental transition when family members take over pioneer hawker stalls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: So, when a subsidised stall is transferred to an immediate family member of the first-generation subsidised rent-holder, we have a special provision to allow him or her to pay subsidised rental rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan
sentences.text: However, for transfers to other family members and relatives, for example, third-generation relatives, we provide a reasonable timeframe of three years for the rent to be staggered from subsidised rent to market rent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan

sentences.speaker: Ms Goh Hanyan

sections.label: ACT 1 funding projects companies

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We also require our public waste collectors to clear the recyclables from the blue bins on a regular schedule, specifically so that the bins do not overflow and to attend to feedback within 24 hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, on behalf of all hon Members who have participated in the MSE Committee of Supply, I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to Minister Grace Fu, Senior Minister of State Zaqy, Senior Minister of State Janil, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh and all members of MSE, PUB, NEA, SFA.
